name: Neckmaxxing / neck training

lead: Neckmaxxing is training the neck muscles to make the neck thicker, which proponents say gives a more masculine, dominant look and better balance between the head, jaw and body. It is described on looksmax.org as a softmaxx.

Neck exercises load the muscles around the cervical spine, with the sternocleidomastoid named in forum guides as the muscle that thickens the neck from the front. Forum posts offer ratio targets, such as neck width to bigonial (jaw) width near 1:1 or a neck-to-height ratio near 1.35, and say a wider neck makes a narrow head and jaw look more in proportion. These are community conventions; no published study validates them and no clinical studies of neck training for appearance were found.

paras: People follow forum guides using neck curls, extensions and similar loaded movements added to a lifting routine, and track neck width with a tape. A thicker neck builds over months of consistent training.
Loaded neck exercises sit near the cervical spine, and one forum guide calls neck work one of the most dangerous softmaxxes. Gradual loading and careful form are the usual precautions in guides.

angle.text: Neckmaxxers train the neck to make it thicker, which they say adds a masculine, dominant look and better face and frame proportions. A wider neck sits more in balance with the jaw and shoulders. Neck-to-jaw ratio targets circulate on forums, and no published study validates them.

lead: Neckmaxxing is the looksmaxxing practice of training the neck to make it thicker, on the belief that a wider neck contributes to a masculine, dominant look and better facial and frame proportions [1][2].

Forum posts offer ideal ratios, such as a neck-to-bigonial (jaw width) ratio of roughly 0.95 to 1, and in one thread a neck width-to-height ratio near 1.35 [1]. Another guide states the neck should match the width of the widest part of the face and that the bigonial to bizygomatic ratio should be around 0.9 to 1.05 [2]. These are community conventions, and no published study validating them was found.
No clinical studies of neck training for appearance were found.
infobox: Neck about equal to bigonial width

paras: Forum guides describe adding neck exercises, such as neck curls and extensions, to a lifting routine. One author calls the neck among the most dangerous yet rewarding softmaxxes and claims it could add about 0.5 PSL points [2]. PSL is a community rating scale for looks and is not a validated measure.

Posters compare necks to celebrity examples and discuss proportions with the head and jaw, saying that people with a small or narrow skull may already be proportional while those with a wide skull would need to build neck size [1]. A guide on the sternocleidomastoid describes keeping the neck 'packed' during curls [2]. A third thread shows before and after posts [3].

The forum material references a PubMed paper on androgen receptor expression in neck and limb muscles, but its findings are not summarized in the posts [1]. No expert guidance on neck thickness for appearance was found.

lore.intro: Neckmaxxing threads on looksmax.org mix anatomy, ratio targets and training guides [1][2].

claims.claim: A neck about as wide as the jaw is ideal.
Neck training can add notable rating points to overall looks.
